about: Living Roots Wine & Co. is the winery of Sebastian and Colleen Hardy, founded in 2016 and split between the Finger Lakes and South Australia. Seb is a sixth-generation winemaker: his ancestor Thomas Hardy arrived in South Australia in 1850 and planted some of its first vines, and his father, Geoff Hardy, planted K1, the first vineyard in Kuitpo, a cool, high subregion at the southern end of the Adelaide Hills. Colleen, from the Rochester area, met Seb while working a vintage in Australia. In 2023 Halliday’s Wine Companion named Living Roots Australia’s Best New Winery.

This red pairs two grapes from the family’s Kuitpo vineyards: Cabernet Sauvignon from Seb’s uncle Bill’s block and Tannat, the famously tannic grape of south-west France and Uruguay, from Geoff’s K1 vineyard. The two were made separately. The Cabernet was destemmed and given two punch-downs a day for a classic extraction, while the Tannat was covered for ten days of carbonic maceration, fermenting inside whole berries to bring out brighter fruit and soften its formidable tannins. The wine then rested in a two-year-old puncheon and older barrels.

The winemakers describe vibrant strawberry and cherry balanced by savoury herbal notes, supple tannins and a spicy finish: a lighter, fresher take on two grapes better known for power. Carbonic maceration is the technique behind the soft, juicy reds of Beaujolais; using it on a grape as tough as Tannat is an unusual and deliberate choice.
facts: Cabernet open-fermented with punch-downs; Tannat 10 days carbonic maceration
